reviewedRiskGates.notes: Scoop-shop menu, linked takeout, and linked delivery are distinct service surfaces.
Official dine-in/location HTML menu is complete enough to enumerate visible named products, but takeout and delivery catalogs are unresolved.
The 25 frozen rows include categories and inaccessible ordering artifacts, while the current official page contains dozens of named products and named service products.
Numerous named current official products have no frozen row.
Frozen ordering products cannot be verified from the failed linked ordering endpoint; the former take-out page label is not a product.

Several flavor names occur in multiple sections/presentations, including Karamel Sutra and Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough; category/presentation must not be collapsed into a single product without retaining the presentation.
Ordering is restaurant-linked vendor evidence and delivery is third-party; neither is restaurant-issued.
Category rows and the shake component string do not constitute exact standalone product matches.
Official guidance discusses labels and changing manufacture but gives no location scoop-shop shared-equipment/cross-contact statement; no cross-contact conclusion is supportable.
Identity and official HTML menu extraction are high confidence; unresolved service catalogs and allergen completeness remain material risks, not low-confidence research.
Luna's material catalog and allergen-disclosure risks are confirmed, while its current-product enumeration is itself incomplete.

findings.summary: Luna's 16 current products include three category headings and two generic section abstractions, while the reopened official location menu lists dozens of named flavors/pints plus five named sundaes and six named shakes.

Frozen exact-match rows contain complete allergen arrays and negative may-contain arrays attributed to official ingredients, but the reopened location menu provides product descriptions rather than current complete allergen declarations. Only narrow named ingredient positives are supportable; no cross-contact conclusion is available.
The linked takeout API returned an error and an official-link Grubhub delivery service was omitted by Luna. Neither unresolved service catalog supports a missing-product or allergen negative.

summary: Identity is verified. Luna correctly found the primary official menu and allergen guidance, but its current catalog is materially underenumerated and mixes categories with products. The official location menu confirms the frozen formula-to-name matches, yet does not support the frozen complete allergen arrays, negative may-contain arrays, or a scoop-shop cross-contact conclusion. Linked takeout and third-party delivery remain unresolved service surfaces.
